strongest_angle: National Geographic published an article in October 2026 detailing Harry Houdini's recently deciphered first diary, a little red book from Dr. Bruce Averbook's collection that illuminates his rise from dime-store vaudeville alongside his wife Bess, coinciding with the centenary of his death on October 31, 1926.

key_facts.fact: National Geographic published an article on October 28, 2026, by author Nina Strochlic about Harry Houdini's recently deciphered first diary, a little red book detailing his rise in vaudeville and the role of his wife Bess.

Dr. Bruce Averbook's collection houses Harry Houdini's earliest known travel diary covering 1897 to 1899, which was annotated by John Cox and published in a book titled Escaping Obscurity: The Travel Diary of Harry Houdini, 1897-1899.

The Averbook Magic Art Museum & Library noted that no diary of Harry Houdini had ever been made public in its entirety prior to the publication of Escaping Obscurity: The Travel Diary of Harry Houdini, 1897-1899 from Dr. Bruce Averbook's collection.
key_facts.source_name: The Averbook Magic Art Museum & Library

key_facts.fact: National Geographic Italia reported on October 30, 2026, that illusionist Harry Houdini died 100 years ago on October 31, 1926, while discussing his newly revealed red pocket diary.
